title: Security Controls and Maintenance
summary: Explains maintenance mode, platform security controls, and sensitive administrative actions.

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: The pentest reset operation is destructive for all non-open-vulnerability pentest rows and associated report references. Export summary data before execution.

sections.title: Security control surface
paragraphs: The security and maintenance area is limited to admin sessions and is additionally blocked when reset-required state is active. This prevents sensitive operations under transitional credential state.
Administrative controls are implemented as explicit endpoints with server-side validation and audit-friendly response payloads.

rows: Rotate privileged credentials under policy checks.
Trigger zone parsing and records refresh on demand.
Clear pentest progress except unresolved vulnerabilities.

sections.title: Password policy and rotation flow
paragraphs: Admin password changes enforce length and common-password restrictions and reject passwords containing the username. New password must differ from the current value.
The UI enforces confirmation matching before request submission, while backend repeats validation to guarantee policy integrity.

rows: Client and backend common password set.
New value must differ from current or temporary password

sections.title: Manual update operation
paragraphs: Manual update calls `update_data()` and refreshes records from configured zone sources. Use this when automation cadence is insufficient for urgent inventory refresh.
A successful call returns `Records updated successfully.`. Failure returns an error payload and requires log review before retry.
orderedList: Wait for completion message and progress bar to clear.
Reopen Records dashboard and validate recent changes in source and status fields.
If failure occurs, inspect backend logs and retry only after root cause is addressed.

sections.title: Pentest reset guardrails and data effects
paragraphs: Reset requires two independent confirmations: checkbox approval and exact phrase match `RESET ALL BUT OPEN VULNERABILITIES`. Requests without both are rejected with `400`.
Rows are preserved only when `vulnerable=1` and `vulnerability_fixed=0`. All other pentest rows are removed, and both manual and generated report files are deleted when present.

rows: Deleted for rows being reset when `report_file` exists.
Deleted for rows being reset when `generated_report_file` exists.

sections.title: Reset summary and CSV interpretation
paragraphs: Before reset, the dialog loads summary data from `GET /pentest/records` and can export a CSV snapshot. This snapshot should be retained as a pre-reset evidence artifact.
After reset, backend returns a stats object that should be reviewed and archived in change notes.

rows: Number of `pentest_data` rows deleted by the reset operation.
Number of unresolved vulnerability rows preserved.

sections.title: Post-maintenance validation checklist
paragraphs: Always validate security and maintenance actions immediately after completion to detect partial failures early and preserve operational confidence.
orderedList: Confirm affected users can still authenticate according to policy.
Validate section visibility for at least one admin and one manager account.
Verify pentest dashboard counts match expected preserved-open-vulnerability totals after reset.
Confirm report download paths for preserved records are intact.
Attach reset summary and CSV snapshot to the change record.
